## Overview
Some customers reconcile Redwood token usage against internal estimates and may observe higher usage totals. The most common causes are (1) client retries and (2) streaming cancellation behavior.
This page provides a support-ready explanation and recommended mitigations.
## Key definitions
- **Attempt**: a single request admitted by the Redwood API gateway (server-side).
- **Logical request**: what the customer thinks of as one user action; may map to multiple attempts if the client retries.
## What we bill
### Retries
- Redwood usage is recorded per-attempt.
- If a client retries after a timeout or non-200 response, each admitted attempt can be billable.
- The Usage dashboard lists rows by **request_id** (attempt identifier)."}, {"source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/usage-accounting-retries-and-stream-cancellation", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Usage accounting: retries and streaming cancellation", "status": "published", "updated": "2025-02-18", "text": "- The Usage dashboard lists rows by **request_id** (attempt identifier).
### Streaming cancellation
- **Prompt tokens** are counted once the request is admitted (even if the client cancels the stream later).
- **Completion tokens** are counted based on tokens actually generated/streamed prior to cancellation.
## Common customer symptoms
- We only sent N requests but we see >N rows: retries created additional attempts.
- We timed out at 15s so we expected zero bill: prompt tokens + partial completion tokens may still be counted.
## Recommended mitigations
1) Avoid automatic retries on client-side timeouts for long generations.
2) Increase client timeout where possible (align to max expected generation time).
3) Reduce max_tokens / output length to meet latency budgets.
4) For troubleshooting, ask for a small set of request_ids + the customers retry/cancel metrics."}, {"source": "confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/free-tier-limits-2025", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Free Tier Limits", "status": "published", "updated": "2025-11-10", "text": "meta: author=Soojin Lee; owner_team=product; created_at=2025-11-03; labels=pricing, free-tier, hosted-api, limits
[body]
## Purpose
What happens when a Free workspace uses up its monthly included usage.
## Limits
- Free includes a fixed monthly amount of billed tokens and requests.
- Free has no overage: nothing beyond the included usage is ever charged, and Free workspaces never get an invoice.
## At the limit
Once a Free workspace reaches its monthly limit, further requests are rate-limited: the API returns HTTP `429` with error code `quota_exceeded` and a `Retry-After` header. Requests work again when the next month starts. To keep sending requests sooner, the customer upgrades to a paid plan.
_Last reviewed 2025-11-10._"}, {"source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/billing-case-routing-and-handoffs", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Billing Support: Case Routing and Handoffs", "status": "published", "updated": "2026-02-06", "text": "- If the customer doesn't have some of the details, hand off with what you have and note what's missing. raj: interesting — `x-cache-status: HIT` and `x-tokens-used: 0` suggests we served from prefix cache but didn't emit billing event. forwarding to billing infra.

marie: oh. that PR was supposed to call meter.emit on cache hits but i see a conditional early-return slipped in. bug."}, {"source": "jira/customer-support/SUP-556901-cache-hit-invoice-line-explanation-and-provisional-credit", "kind": "case record or discussion", "title": "SUP-556901: Invoice shows separate 'cache-hit tokens' line plus 'generated tokens' for same time window — clarification and potential adjustment requested", "status": "In Progress", "updated": "2026-03-03", "text": "[investigation_notes]
Reviewed change log for metering pipeline: PR #1898 added a distinct meter for kv cache hits to enable more granular telemetry and cost attribution for hosted customers.
